parties: Rainbow Investments Limited; Spencer's Retail Limited
headline: Rainbow Investments Limited files Regulation 31(4) disclosure with NSE for substantial acquisition in Spencer's Retail
sum: Rainbow Investments Limited has filed a Regulation 31(4) disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations with NSE, signalling a substantial acquisition triggering open-market disclosure obligations for Spencer's Retail Limited, a publicly listed retail chain.
implication: Regulation 31(4) filings mark the entry into public acquisition territory-once crossed, the acquirer is bound by mandatory offer, creeping acquisition caps, and fair-value fairness opinion requirements; Spencer's shareholders and the market now have visibility into a material shareholding movement.
detail: Rainbow Investments Limited has submitted to NSE a disclosure under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, concerning Spencer's Retail Limited. This disclosure is required when an entity's shareholding in a listed company crosses prescribed thresholds (typically 5% or 10% depending on existing holding), triggering mandatory open-market notification and potential full or partial offer obligations. The filing signals entry into the structured takeover framework and activates compliance with SEBI's fair-value, independent director, and disclosure timelines.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 - Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure requirement when shareholding crosses thresholds; defines timing, content and exchange filing obligations.
Establishes the 5%, 10%, 15%, 25%, 35%, 50%, 75% threshold tiers and their trigger events.
Once thresholds breached, defines who must make an open offer, timing (6 weeks), pricing, and exemptions.
Limits acquisition pace above certain thresholds (e.g., 5% per financial year in secondary market if holding >25%).

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013 - Sections 149, 152 (Board composition, director appointment)
framework.note: Acquirer gaining control may need to appoint directors; disclosure triggers Nomination & Remuneration Committee review.

framework.ref: Listing Regulations (SEBI) - Regulations 30, 33 (Material Information, Corporate Governance)
framework.note: Spencer's board must immediately disclose material information; SEBI Reg. 33 governs fair-value determination by independent valuers.

framework.ref: SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011 - Regulation 4 (Exemptions, Category I–IV)
framework.note: Specific exemptions for related-party acquisitions, employee stock plans, or government/institutional acquirers may apply; requires case-by-case review.

framework.ref: Insider Trading (Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations, 2015 - Regulation 3
framework.note: Rainbow Investments and related parties subject to Chinese Wall, trading window closures, and disclosures under Schedule A-II once acquisition intent is known.

conditions: Regulatory disclosure under Regulation 31(4) filed; open-market threshold crossed.
Potential mandatory open offer obligation contingent on final shareholding analysis and applicable exemptions.
approvals: Potential CCI approval if acquisition value/combined turnover triggers merger control thresholds (Section 5(a) Competition Act, 2002).

triggers.law: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011
triggers.note: Regulation 31(4) disclosure triggers once shareholding crosses notifiable threshold; defines fair-value determination, offer timing, and public dissemination.
If combined turnover of acquirer + Spencer's exceeds ₹2,250 cr (as of FY2026 thresholds), CCI pre-approval required before acquisition completion.
Acquisition intent triggers trading window closure for Spencer's insiders and Chinese Wall protocols for Rainbow and advisors.

firms.note: Legal advisors not disclosed in primary source; typically investment banker / M&A counsel would advise on fair-value opinion and open-offer mechanics.
Spencer's board and independent directors will appoint valuers and legal counsel for fair-value fairness opinion and shareholder communication.
